name: Ivermectin cream
lead: Ivermectin 1% (10 mg/g) cream, marketed as Soolantra, is a topical antiparasitic approved for papulopustular rosacea.[1][2] It is applied once daily to the face.[3]

Researchers have proposed that it acts both on Demodex mites and through anti-inflammatory effects; laboratory work found it reduced expression of the innate-immune mediators LL-37 and KLK5 in skin models.[4] A systematic review and meta-analysis examined its efficacy and quality-of-life impact.[5]
No looksmaxxing-community material was found for this entry; it appears here because of rosacea redness and bumps.

paras: Topical ivermectin is used for inflammatory lesions of papulopustular rosacea.[3] Case series and small studies have also looked at ocular rosacea and Demodex infestation of the eyelids.[6]
It has been described as complementary to oral modified-release doxycycline 40 mg, since the two target different inflammatory pathways.[2]
Rosacea involves elevated cathelicidin peptides such as LL-37 and the protease KLK5; ivermectin cream reduced their gene expression in reconstructed and ex vivo skin models.[4]

A Phase 3 trial (962 participants) compared ivermectin 1% cream with metronidazole 0.75% cream in papulopustular rosacea.[7] A systematic review and meta-analysis assessed topical ivermectin 1% against other topicals on efficacy and quality of life.[5] A 34-patient case series reported results from clinical practice.[8]
Additional registered trials cover bioequivalence of generic creams and Demodex-related conditions.[9]

card.summary: Prescription antiparasitic cream approved for rosacea bumps, backed by Phase 3 trials.
card.note: Prescription product; unrelated to oral ivermectin use debates.

quick.overview:
Ivermectin 1% cream (Soolantra) is a prescription once-daily topical for papulopustular rosacea.

It has been compared against metronidazole cream in a large Phase 3 trial and reviewed in a meta-analysis.
quick.mechanism: It is thought to act on Demodex mites and to reduce inflammatory signals such as LL-37 and KLK5 in the skin.
quick.risks: Adverse-event details are in the trial and label data. It is a prescription topical, distinct from oral ivermectin.
